standard_prerequisites.name: For K-flat K and any complex L there is a canonical map K -> Hom(L, Tot(K tensor L))
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the first arrow of the composite defining the morphism.

core_obligations: The statement is a special case of the internal-hom-diagonal-better lemma with M = A, but the proof also gives it directly (proof lines 18840-18841): represent K by a K-flat complex K and L by any complex L, choose a quasi-isomorphism Tot(K tensor L) -> J with J K-injective (proof lines 18842-18845). The composite K -> Hom(L, Tot(K tensor L)) -> Hom(L, J), whose first arrow is the diagonal map, defines in D(R) a morphism K -> RHom_R(L, K tensor L); K-injectivity of J makes the target compute the derived internal hom, and functoriality in K and L follows from the functoriality of the diagonal map and of the resolution (proof lines 18846-18851).
proof_roadmap: Note the special-case route, then choose representatives and a K-injective resolution (proof lines 18840-18845).
Define the morphism via the diagonal map into the Hom into the resolution (proof lines 18846-18851).
